why:
rclcpp_action puts the action entities in their OWN namespace, so they can be called `Client<ActionT>` and `Server<ActionT>` beside `rclcpp::Client`. We ship one namespace, `nros`, where `Client` is already the service client -- so ours are `nros::ActionClient<A>` / `nros::ActionServer<A>` and every rclcpp_action member correlates as theirs-only even where we have it. So `rclcpp_action::Server<ActionT>` and its members read as theirs-only even though `nros::ActionServer<A>` implements most of them. The genuinely absent parts are the `Waitable` members (`execute`, `is_ready`, `set_on_ready_callback`, `clear_on_ready_callback`) -- rcl's wait-set protocol -- the caller asks each entity how many wait-set slots it needs and then reads back which of them are ready. RFC-0002's executor drives entities directly through the RMW vtable, so there is no wait set. See the pubsub and service stages' identical rows. -- and `make_shared`, which needs an allocator.

phase-428 W6 (2026-09-06) — disposition, required because this row's SHAPE CORRESPONDS: the name exists on the ported surface and the correlator files it `same`, so nothing in a build says the contract differs. That is the class RFC-0089 exists for.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp_action::Server<ActionT>` is obtained from `rclcpp_action::create_server(...)` as a `SharedPtr` and is a `Waitable` — `execute`, `is_ready`, `set_on_ready_callback`, `clear_on_ready_callback` — driven by rcl's wait set.

OURS: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp_action/server.hpp` — `template <typename A> class Server`, the DEFINITION (phase-428 moved it here from `nros::ActionServer`). The type NAME is upstream's; what it names is our action server, which RFC-0002's executor drives directly through the RMW vtable, so there is no wait set to participate in and no allocator for `make_shared`.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: COMPILE ERROR, member by member — the type name resolves and every member upstream has and we do not is `no member named ... in 'nros::ActionServer<A>'`. Nothing about this alias compiles and differs; it adopts a name for the same concept with a smaller member set, which is ADOPT-BOUNDED.

phase-428 (RFC-0089): THE OPEN QUESTION THIS ROW LEFT IS ANSWERED. The definition moved to `rclcpp_action::Client<A>` / `rclcpp_action::Server<A>` and `nros::ActionClient<A>` / `nros::ActionServer<A>` became the migration aliases -- so the constraint the paragraph above describes ("we ship one namespace, `nros`, where `Client` is already the service client") no longer holds: we ship `rclcpp_action` too, and the action client is `Client` there beside `rclcpp::Client`. What remains ours is the STORAGE shape, not the NAME.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it: the class doc comment on `rclcpp_action::Server<A>` now lists the three things upstream's has and this does not — no `Waitable` members, no `create_server`/`SharedPtr` creation (initialised in place by `node.create_action_server`), no `ServerGoalHandle` — and the porting guide's action row, which said "The action call shapes (send_goal_async etc.) match" (false), now points at an Actions section stating the same. Its other claim, that `rclcpp_action::Server/Client` are "aliases for `nros::ActionServer/Client<A>`", had the alias backwards since phase-428 and is corrected too.
